objects.description: Structure holding floating-point Euler angles: roll, pitch, yaw (in radians or degrees depending on usage elsewhere; header does not specify). Used as the structured view of fp_angles_t union.
Union providing two views of a 3-axis attitude: as raw[3] floats or as named angles (roll, pitch, yaw) via fp_angles_def.
Online standard deviation/variance accumulator storing running means (old/new), sum of squares (old/new), and count. Works with devClear/devPush/devVariance/devStandardDeviation functions.
Sample item for a filter-with-buffer implementation, containing a value and its timestamp.
State for a buffered filter: holds buffer length, current index, and pointer to an array of filterWithBufferSample_t samples. Allocation/ownership of samples is not specified here.
Working state for sensor calibration linear system solving (accumulate X^T*Y and X^T*X). Used with sensorCalibration* API to push samples and solve for offset/scale.
Element type for bit arrays operated on by bitarray.h helpers. Arrays should be 4-byte aligned. Represents a 32-bit storage unit.

functions.name: sensorCalibrationResetState
functions.description: Reset/initialize the sensor calibration accumulator/state prior to pushing samples. Typical usage: call once before collecting samples for either offset or scale solutions.
requirements: state must be a valid, writable pointer to a sensorCalibrationState_t.
Call before using other sensorCalibration* functions for a fresh calibration cycle.
Thread-safety is unknown; do not share state across threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: sensorCalibrationPushSampleForOffsetCalculation
functions.description: Accumulate a single 3-axis sample for computing sensor offset (bias). Use after reset and before solving for offset.
requirements: state must be a valid, writable pointer initialized via sensorCalibrationResetState.
sample must point to at least 3 floats representing a single 3D measurement.
Call repeatedly with multiple samples to obtain a solvable system; minimum count unknown.
Do not modify state concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: sensorCalibrationPushSampleForScaleCalculation
functions.signature: void sensorCalibrationPushSampleForScaleCalculation(sensorCalibrationState_t * state, int axis, float sample[3], int target);
functions.description: Accumulate a single 3-axis sample for computing scale (gain) on a specified axis, likely relative to a known target magnitude/value.
requirements: state must be initialized with sensorCalibrationResetState.
sample must point to at least 3 floats.
axis should identify the axis index; valid range is inferred as 0..2 (unknown if other values are accepted).
target is the expected value for the specified axis; units/scale are domain-specific and not documented.
Provide sufficient samples before solving; exact minimum unknown.
Do not modify state concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: sensorCalibrationSolveForOffset
functions.description: Solve the accumulated system to estimate 3-axis offset (bias). Returns true on success and writes the 3-element result vector.
requirements: state must contain samples pushed via sensorCalibrationPushSampleForOffsetCalculation.
result must point to at least 3 writable floats.
Returns false if the system is underdetermined or numerically singular; caller should handle a false return.
Do not pass a null state or result.

functions.name: sensorCalibrationSolveForScale
functions.description: Solve the accumulated system to estimate per-axis scale (gain). Returns true on success and writes the 3-element result vector.
requirements: state must contain samples pushed via sensorCalibrationPushSampleForScaleCalculation.
result must point to at least 3 writable floats.
Returns false if insufficient/ill-conditioned data; handle false.
Do not pass a null state or result.

functions.name: gcd
functions.description: Compute the greatest common divisor of two integers. Typical usage for reducing ratios or normalizing fractions.
requirements: denom should not be 0; behavior for zero or negative inputs is unspecified.
If either argument is negative, sign of the return value is unspecified (commonly non-negative).
Inputs should be finite integers.

functions.name: applyDeadband
functions.description: Apply a symmetric deadband to value, typically returning 0 when |value| <= deadband and passing through otherwise (exact rescaling specifics unknown).
requirements: deadband should be non-negative.
No overflow guarantees are given; large values could overflow depending on implementation.
Behavior is unspecified for negative deadband.

functions.name: applyDeadbandRescaled
functions.signature: int32_t applyDeadbandRescaled(int32_t value, int32_t deadband, int32_t min, int32_t max);
functions.description: Apply a deadband to value and rescale the remaining range to [min,max] (exact mapping policy is not documented).
requirements: deadband should be non-negative.
min and max define the output scale; the function name suggests min <= max; behavior if min > max is unspecified.
Value range before/after rescaling is unspecified; caller should ensure inputs near limits are acceptable.

functions.name: constrain
functions.signature: int32_t constrain(int32_t amt, int32_t low, int32_t high);
functions.description: Clamp amt to the inclusive range [low, high].
requirements: low should be <= high; if not, behavior is implementation-defined/unknown.

functions.name: constrainf
functions.signature: float constrainf(float amt, float low, float high);
functions.description: Clamp amt to the inclusive range [low, high] in floating point.
requirements: low should be <= high; if not, behavior is implementation-defined/unknown.
amt, low, and high should be finite floats to avoid NaN propagation.

functions.name: devClear
functions.description: Initialize/clear an online standard deviation/variance accumulator state prior to pushing samples.
requirements: dev must be a valid, writable pointer.
Call before devPush/devVariance/devStandardDeviation for a new dataset.

functions.name: devPush
functions.description: Push a new sample x into the running variance/standard-deviation accumulator.
requirements: dev must have been initialized with devClear.
Input x should be finite; NaN/Inf handling is unspecified.
Not thread-safe without external synchronization.

functions.name: devVariance
functions.description: Return the current variance from the accumulator dev.
requirements: dev must have been initialized and have at least 1–2 samples; exact minimum for a non-zero variance is typically >=2 but not documented.
Return value for insufficient samples is unspecified (commonly 0).

functions.name: devStandardDeviation
functions.description: Return the current standard deviation from the accumulator dev.
requirements: dev must have been initialized and have enough samples for a meaningful result (commonly >=2).
Result for insufficient samples is unspecified (commonly 0).

functions.name: degreesToRadians
functions.description: Convert degrees to radians and return as float.
requirements: Input degrees should be within int16_t range.
No special constraints; returns finite float for finite input.

functions.name: scaleRange
functions.signature: int scaleRange(int x, int srcMin, int srcMax, int destMin, int destMax);
functions.description: Linearly map x from [srcMin, srcMax] into [destMin, destMax].
requirements: srcMin and srcMax must not be equal to avoid division by zero.
Mapping for x outside [srcMin, srcMax] is linear extrapolation; caller should ensure this is acceptable.
All inputs should be finite integers.

functions.name: scaleRangef
functions.signature: float scaleRangef(float x, float srcMin, float srcMax, float destMin, float destMax);
functions.description: Linearly map x from [srcMin, srcMax] into [destMin, destMax] in floating point.
requirements: srcMin and srcMax must not be equal.
Inputs should be finite floats to avoid NaN/Inf results.
Behavior for x outside source range is linear extrapolation.

functions.name: wrap_18000
functions.description: Wrap an angle in centidegrees to the range [-18000, 18000) (inferred from name).
requirements: angle is in centidegrees; units are assumed.
Exact bounds and handling of limits are inferred; implementation details unknown.

functions.name: wrap_180
functions.description: Wrap an angle in degrees to the range [-180, 180) (inferred from name).
requirements: angle is in degrees.
Exact edge behavior (e.g., 180) is inferred; implementation details unknown.

functions.name: wrap_36000
functions.description: Wrap an angle in centidegrees to the range [0, 36000) (inferred from name).
requirements: angle is in centidegrees.
Exact edge behavior is inferred; implementation details unknown.

functions.name: quickMedianFilter3
functions.description: Return the median of a 3-sample int32 window quickly. Likely operates on v[0..2].
requirements: v must point to at least 3 int32_t elements.
Alignment/aliasing requirements are standard for int32_t pointers.
Behavior with fewer than 3 elements is invalid.

functions.name: quickMedianFilter5
functions.description: Return the median of a 5-sample int32 window. Likely uses v[0..4].
requirements: v must point to at least 5 int32_t elements.

functions.name: quickMedianFilter7
functions.description: Return the median of a 7-sample int32 window. Likely uses v[0..6].
requirements: v must point to at least 7 int32_t elements.

functions.name: quickMedianFilter9
functions.description: Return the median of a 9-sample int32 window. Likely uses v[0..8].
requirements: v must point to at least 9 int32_t elements.

functions.name: quickMedianFilter3_16
functions.description: Return the median of a 3-sample int16 window. Likely uses v[0..2].
requirements: v must point to at least 3 int16_t elements.

functions.name: quickMedianFilter5_16
functions.description: Return the median of a 5-sample int16 window. Likely uses v[0..4].
requirements: v must point to at least 5 int16_t elements.

functions.name: sin_approx
functions.description: Fast sine approximation of x (radians). Controlled by FAST_MATH/VERY_FAST_MATH compile-time selection.
requirements: x is in radians.
Accuracy and valid input range are approximation-dependent; large |x| may reduce accuracy.
Available only when FAST_MATH or VERY_FAST_MATH is defined in this header.

functions.name: cos_approx
functions.description: Fast cosine approximation of x (radians).
requirements: x is in radians.
Approximation accuracy varies; large |x| may reduce accuracy.
Available only when FAST_MATH or VERY_FAST_MATH is defined.

functions.name: atan2_approx
functions.description: Fast approximation of atan2(y, x), returning the angle in radians.
requirements: Inputs should be finite floats.
Behavior when both x and y are 0 is unspecified.
Available only when FAST_MATH or VERY_FAST_MATH is defined.

functions.name: acos_approx
functions.description: Fast approximation of arccos(x), returning radians.
requirements: Domain is typically x in [-1, 1]; outside this range behavior is unspecified.
Available only when FAST_MATH or VERY_FAST_MATH is defined.

functions.name: arraySubInt32
functions.signature: void arraySubInt32(int32_t *dest, int32_t *array1, int32_t *array2, int count);
functions.description: Compute element-wise subtraction: dest[i] = array1[i] - array2[i] for i in [0, count).
requirements: dest, array1, and array2 must be valid pointers to at least count int32_t elements.
count must be non-negative; if zero, function performs no operation.
Aliasing/overlap behavior is unspecified; use non-overlapping buffers for safety.

functions.name: bellCurve
functions.signature: float bellCurve(const float x, const float curveWidth);
functions.description: Compute a bell-curve-like weighting function of x with a width parameter. Exact formula not documented; likely centered at 0 with width controlling spread.
requirements: curveWidth should be positive to avoid division by zero or degenerate output.
Inputs should be finite floats.

functions.name: attenuation
functions.signature: float attenuation(const float input, const float width);
functions.description: Compute an attenuation factor based on input and width (details not documented). Likely returns a [0,1]-like weight decreasing with |input|.
requirements: width should be positive.
Inputs should be finite floats.

functions.name: gaussian
functions.signature: float gaussian(const float x, const float mu, const float sigma);
functions.description: Evaluate a Gaussian function at x with mean mu and standard deviation sigma. Returns exp(-0.5 * ((x-mu)/sigma)^2) scaled by 1/(sigma*sqrt(2π)) or a normalized variant (exact normalization unspecified).
requirements: sigma must be > 0 to avoid division by zero.
Inputs should be finite floats.

functions.name: fast_fsqrtf
functions.description: Fast approximation of square root of value.
requirements: value should be >= 0 for real results; behavior for negative inputs is unspecified.
Input should be a finite float.

functions.name: calc_length_pythagorean_2D
functions.signature: float calc_length_pythagorean_2D(const float firstElement, const float secondElement);
functions.description: Compute the 2D Euclidean length sqrt(x^2 + y^2).
requirements: Inputs should be finite floats to avoid NaNs.
May overflow/underflow if inputs are extremely large/small; no special scaling is documented.

functions.name: calc_length_pythagorean_3D
functions.signature: float calc_length_pythagorean_3D(const float firstElement, const float secondElement, const float thirdElement);
functions.description: Compute the 3D Euclidean length sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2).
requirements: Inputs should be finite floats.
No overflow/underflow protection is documented.

functions.name: bitArrayGet
functions.description: Return the boolean value of the specified bit index in a 4-byte-aligned bit array.
requirements: array must point to a bit array declared with BITARRAY_DECLARE or otherwise 4-byte aligned.
bit must be within the bounds of the allocated array; no size parameter is provided, so the caller must ensure validity.
Pointer must be readable.

functions.name: bitArraySet
functions.description: Set the specified bit in a 4-byte-aligned bit array.
requirements: array must be 4-byte aligned (use BITARRAY_DECLARE).
bit must be within bounds of the allocated array.
Pointer must be writable.

functions.name: bitArrayClr
functions.description: Clear the specified bit in a 4-byte-aligned bit array.
requirements: array must be 4-byte aligned (use BITARRAY_DECLARE).
bit must be within bounds of the allocated array.
Pointer must be writable.

functions.name: bitArraySetAll
functions.description: Set all bits in the bit array to 1. The size parameter is the size of the array in bytes.
requirements: array must be 4-byte aligned (use BITARRAY_DECLARE).
size must equal the size in bytes of the underlying array; prefer using BITARRAY_SET_ALL(array) macro to avoid mistakes.
Pointer must be writable.

functions.name: bitArrayClrAll
functions.description: Clear all bits in the bit array to 0. The size parameter is the size of the array in bytes.
requirements: array must be 4-byte aligned (use BITARRAY_DECLARE).
size must equal the size in bytes of the underlying array; prefer using BITARRAY_CLR_ALL(array) macro.
Pointer must be writable.

functions.name: bitArrayFindFirstSet
functions.signature: int bitArrayFindFirstSet(const bitarrayElement_t *array, unsigned start_bit, size_t size);
functions.description: Return the index of the first set bit at or after start_bit, or -1 if none. Size must be the array size in bytes.
requirements: array must be 4-byte aligned (use BITARRAY_DECLARE).
size must equal the size in bytes of the array; prefer BITARRAY_FIND_FIRST_SET(array, start_bit).
start_bit may be any value; if >= total bits, -1 is returned.
Pointer must be readable.

functions.name: arm_sub_f32
functions.signature: void arm_sub_f32(float * pSrcA, float * pSrcB, float * pDst, uint32_t blockSize);
functions.description: Element-wise subtraction: pDst[i] = pSrcA[i] - pSrcB[i] for i in [0, blockSize). Provided for SITL builds as a replacement for CMSIS-DSP.
requirements: Available only when SITL_BUILD is defined.
pSrcA, pSrcB, and pDst must point to at least blockSize floats.
blockSize is the number of elements to process.
Buffers should be non-overlapping or safely handled; overlap behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: arm_scale_f32
functions.signature: void arm_scale_f32(float * pSrc, float scale, float * pDst, uint32_t blockSize);
functions.description: Element-wise scaling: pDst[i] = pSrc[i] * scale for i in [0, blockSize). Provided for SITL builds.
requirements: Available only when SITL_BUILD is defined.
pSrc and pDst must point to at least blockSize floats.
blockSize is the number of elements to process.
Overlap behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: arm_mult_f32
functions.signature: void arm_mult_f32(float * pSrcA, float * pSrcB, float * pDst, uint32_t blockSize);
functions.description: Element-wise multiplication: pDst[i] = pSrcA[i] * pSrcB[i] for i in [0, blockSize). Provided for SITL builds.
requirements: Available only when SITL_BUILD is defined.
pSrcA, pSrcB, and pDst must point to at least blockSize floats.
blockSize is the number of elements to process.
Overlap behavior is unspecified.
